tonight.headline: Your 77% is still a read on their empty lineup, not on your roster.
body: Nothing has kicked off on either side. KEI returns have five starters set and four slots empty — both wide receiver spots, the defence and the kicker — with Drake London, George Pickens, the 49ers D/ST and Evan McPherson sitting on their bench. That is where the 121.1 to 70.8 comes from.

If they set their lineup before Sunday morning, roughly forty points arrive on their side and this becomes a normal game. Do not plan around the 77%. Your own lineup is correct as it stands and there is nothing to fire today.

case.label: What the 70.8 is actually made of
case.body: Jaxson Dart at quarterback, De'Von Achane and Cam Skattebo at running back, Tyler Warren at tight end and Travis Etienne in the flex. Five real starters. The other four slots score zero unless someone fills them.

case.label: Where your own points come from
case.body: Jonathan Taylor and Rashee Rice are both in Sunday night's Colts–Chiefs game, which is 38% of your projected total in one window. Taylor is a road underdog by 6.5 with an implied team total of 21.0.

case.label: What you can do about it
case.body: Nothing about their lineup, and nothing about yours. The only live decision in this league closes at 01:00 tonight, and the answer to it is no — see Rico Dowdle in Do not chase.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: KEI returns filling four slots. Their bench holds two starting-calibre receivers and a top-ten defence, so the 77% is a snapshot of an unset lineup and nothing more.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — do not fire this. Lawrence locks Sunday 14:05
doFirst.title: Stafford in for Lawrence — this brief told you to do it on Thursday and it is still wrong
doFirst.subtitle: Rendered unarmed for the second run running. Trevor Lawrence keeps slot 0. Tonight's Rams worksheet strengthens the reversal rather than weakening it.

case.label: What the original card said
case.body: Thursday night's brief told you to start Stafford over Lawrence on ESPN's season projection, which has Stafford 286.4 to Lawrence 282.0. That is a four-point gap across seventeen games, and it was the whole argument.

case.label: What the tape says
case.body: Sharp Football Analysis on Stafford's Week 1: 15 of 25 for 155 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. Lawrence, per FantasyPros' Primer, 'shredded this pass defence last year to the tune of a QB2 finish for the week' and goes back to Denver on Sunday. Yahoo's Week 2 board has Lawrence QB8 and Stafford QB14.

case.label: The schedule argument nobody made
case.body: Stafford plays Monday night. Lawrence plays Sunday at 14:05. Starting Stafford means committing on Saturday to a quarterback who throws forty-eight hours later, with no ability to change your mind once Lawrence's game is in the books. That asymmetry is worth more than four season-projection points on its own.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Stafford outscores Lawrence on Monday night. That would say ESPN's season projection was the better instrument two weeks into a season and this reversal was churn dressed as research — close it WRONG and stop reversing this seat.

doFirst.sources: Sharp Football Analysis · FantasyPros Week 2 Primer · Yahoo Sports · ESPN

whatWentWrong.title: This brief told you to start Stafford over Lawrence on a projection, and never looked at either game
whatWentWrong.lead: Thursday's card was built on a four-point season-projection gap. Stafford went 15 of 25 for 155 with no touchdowns and a pick in Week 1.

case.label: What it cost
case.body: Nothing yet — you did not fire it, and Lawrence is still in slot 0. The cost is that this seat has now been argued three different ways in three days, which is how a lineup gets churned into a worse one.

case.label: The rule it broke
case.body: STRATEGY section 4 and the runbook say the same thing: a projection narrows the list you research, it never decides. A season total for a quarterback a fortnight into the year is the least reliable number on the page.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Monday night. If Stafford beats Lawrence, the reversal was the error rather than the original card, and the honest thing is to log this entry as wrong in turn.

whatWentWrong.title: Four names through one bench seat in three days, and the last one was a quarterback you already had
whatWentWrong.lead: Zach Charbonnet out and Tyler Allgeier in on Friday 16:29. Allgeier out and Matthew Stafford in at 07:12 this morning. Cam Little out and Jason Myers in on Friday 07:06.

case.label: The sequence
case.body: Your own activity log, last seventy-two hours: WAIVER on Charbonnet, add Allgeier, drop Allgeier, add Stafford, drop Little, add Myers. Three seats, six transactions, and the net result is a backup quarterback behind a starter this brief now tells you not to bench.

case.label: Why it connects to the card above
case.body: Stafford is on this roster because Thursday's brief wanted him starting. The card is now a ghost, which means the roster spot was spent acquiring a player the brief immediately stopped recommending. That is the churn rule failing in the most literal way available.

case.label: What it closes
case.body: All three of those seats — quarterback, kicker and the fourth running-back spot — are shut until Tuesday 22 September under the seven-day churn rule. That is most of why Do-first is empty tonight, and it is the correct reason for it to be empty.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A player in one of those seats being ruled out. That is the only condition in STRATEGY section 3 that reopens a slot inside seven days.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +2.5 a week on the lineup they actually have set — Tuten replaces Rachaad White, who they are starting at 7.6 — and +40.6 across the season against your +11.6. Put the number in the message; it is what gets it read.

youGet.name: Lamar Jackson
youGet.detail: QB BAL · 20.8 this week · 312.9 season · QB1 overall

case.label: Why they should say yes
case.body: Team 13 carry Josh Allen at slot 0 and Lamar Jackson at slot 20 in a one-quarterback league. Lamar scores them zero every week he sits there. Meanwhile their second starting running back is Rachaad White at 7.6 — a 27-snap committee body in Washington — with Blake Corum behind him on the bench. Tuten walks into that slot and their optimal season lineup rises 40.6.

case.label: Why you should say yes
case.body: You start one quarterback and it is Trevor Lawrence at QB8. Lamar is QB1 overall. Tuten is your fourth running back behind Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley, and he cannot reach your lineup while Matthew Golden holds the flex on a 30% target share. You are converting a bench body into the best quarterback in football: +3.4 this week, +11.6 across the season.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: Two of them. Tuten is genuinely good — FantasyPros call him a must-start this week on a 46.9% carry share — so this is not a salvage trade, and if Taylor or Barkley goes down you will want him back. And the season arithmetic rests on seasonProj, which has returned the identical +40.6 since 17 September; if that field is a frozen preseason artifact then the +11.6 is August's opinion and only the +3.4 weekly number is real.

case.label: Why LONGSHOT and not EVEN
case.body: This brief labelled it EVEN for three straight runs and was wrong each time. A manager who has held two elite quarterbacks through two weeks and a bye-less schedule has shown you what he thinks. Downgraded on his revealed behaviour, not on the arithmetic.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second real running back, which kills their +40.6. Or they move a quarterback, which kills the surplus. Or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report — he is not on the Week 2 one, which lists only Flowers, Stanley, Simpson and Hendrickson.

trades.sources: ESPN league file · FantasyPros Week 2 Primer · Baltimore Ravens official injury report
trades.copyText: Hey — you're carrying Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson in a one-QB league, so Lamar scores you nothing every Sunday he sits. I'd give you Bhayshul Tuten for him. Straight up. He's Jacksonville's lead back — 46.9% carry share in Week 1 and FantasyPros have him as a must-start this week — and he'd slot straight in over Rachaad White, who's splitting a three-man backfield in Washington. By my math it's worth about +40 to your season total and about +12 to mine, so you're getting the better end and I'm fine with that because I need a QB and you don't. Interested?

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: Still the best free agent in this league for a roster whose flex takes a tight end, and still declined — on the seat, not the player.

case.label: The role
case.body: FantasyLife have him as Minnesota's number two target behind Justin Jefferson at an 81% route share and a 16% target share. He is a free agent here at 65.1% national ownership, which means no waiver priority is at stake — only a roster move.

case.label: What changed tonight, against him
case.body: Kyler Murray is out with a concussion and Carson Wentz starts. Sports Illustrated's fallout piece says flatly that Wentz cannot support two viable receivers, and Wentz's own projection is 183 passing yards. A tight end is third in that queue behind Jefferson.

case.label: Why there is still no seat
case.body: Every bench slot is either just churned or genuinely occupied: the quarterback and kicker seats changed hands in the last 72 hours, Mayer is held while Bowers is doubtful, Vele played 82 snaps and scored, and MarShawn Lloyd now leads a Green Bay backfield whose starter is on the Commissioner's Exempt List. There is no bad player to drop.

case.label: When to act
case.body: The Lamar trade landing or being formally dead, which frees Tuten's seat either way. Or Colston Loveland drawing under four targets against Minnesota on Sunday — that is his own thesis breaking, and Hockenson becomes the answer rather than a discovery.

worthALook.name: Jake Ferguson
worthALook.lead: 81.4% rostered nationally and a free agent here. The highest-owned player on this wire who costs nothing to acquire.

case.label: Why he is free here
case.body: He cleared waivers in this league unclaimed on 17 September and reverted to free agent, so STRATEGY section 6 no longer applies at all — there is no priority cost, only a roster move. That is the cheapest version of the strongest wire signal there is.

case.label: The matchup nobody should ignore
case.body: Dallas host Washington in a game where the Cowboys rank last in the league in third-down defence and have already lost safety Malik Hooker to a fractured forearm. That is a game with points in it on both sides.

case.label: Why he is still not added
case.body: Same answer as Hockenson: no droppable seat, and you already carry two tight ends in a league whose flex takes one. Adding a third would mean cutting Mayer while Bowers is doubtful, which is the one branch the Mayer thesis explicitly forbids.

case.label: When to act
case.body: CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens appearing on a Dallas injury report makes Ferguson the best free agent in the league and the seat becomes worth finding. Or Loveland's four-target clause tripping on Sunday.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: Downgraded tonight. The ownership anomaly is real; Sunday at Denver is the wrong week to test it.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on this wire, 76.8% rostered nationally, free agent here. NBC confirmed Thursday that the thumb will not keep him out.

case.label: The number that argues against acting
case.body: 8.7% target share in Week 1, WR28 for the week. FantasyPros note Denver allowed the second-fewest yards per target and the fewest fantasy points per target to perimeter receivers last season — and Jacksonville's target tree already runs through Brian Thomas Jr. and Travis Hunter.

case.label: The concentration problem
case.body: You already own Trevor Lawrence and Bhayshul Tuten. A third Jacksonville player makes Week 7 worse, when STRATEGY section 8 flags the Jaguars bye as this roster's known structural hole.

case.label: When to act
case.body: A clean Week 2 line on a freed seat. If the Lamar trade lands, Tuten leaves, the Jacksonville concentration halves and this becomes a straightforward add rather than a trade-off.

worthALook.sources: FantasyPros Week 2 Primer · NBC Sports · STRATEGY.md section 8

doNotChase.name: Rico Dowdle
doNotChase.lead: The only live deadline in this league closes at 01:00 tonight, and the answer is no — both to the claim and, correcting this morning's card, to adding him free afterwards.

case.label: What is actually happening at 01:00
case.body: Furia Regia dropped him at 05:39 this morning to add Deebo Samuel. He sits on WAIVERS with clearsAt 07:00Z on 20 September, which is 01:00 Sunday in Mexico City. He is 85.6% rostered nationally with the highest running-back season projection on this wire at 188.9, and he leads Pittsburgh's backfield: 57.8% of snaps and 48.8% of routes in Week 1 against Jaylen Warren's 35.9% and 30.2%.

case.label: Why the claim is still refused
case.body: IPADE priority never resets. You sit at waiverRank 3 and one claim drops you to last for the rest of the season. STRATEGY section 6 spends that only on a player who starts immediately or wins a league. Dowdle would be your fourth running back behind Jonathan Taylor, Saquon Barkley and Tuten — and Sports Illustrated has him RB27, behind Warren at RB24, on a near-even Pittsburgh split. That is not a starter-level need.

case.label: Correcting this morning's card
case.body: The 13:35 brief said that if he cleared unclaimed he should be added free over Devaughn Vele. That was wrong and it was wrong because Vele was never researched. Vele caught seven of nine for 69 and a touchdown on a team-high 82 snaps in Week 1, and Jordyn Tyson is out at least three more games. He is the Saints' clear second option, not a spare body.

case.label: And there is no other seat either
case.body: The alternatives are worse. MarShawn Lloyd projects 11.2 to Dowdle's 10.1 — a move that lowers projected points, which STRATEGY calls a hard floor — and Josh Jacobs being on the Commissioner's Exempt List means Lloyd's role is growing while Dowdle's is a 50-50 split. Mayer is held for Bowers, and the quarterback seat changed hands twelve hours ago. Free is not the same as worth a seat.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley appearing on an injury report. That turns Dowdle from a fourth back into a starter-level need, which is the one condition STRATEGY section 6 accepts — and after 01:00 he would be a free agent, so it would cost nothing but the seat.

doNotChase.sources: Sports Illustrated/OnSI · FantasyPros Week 2 Primer · Bleacher Report · ESPN league activity log · STRATEGY.md section 6

doNotChase.name: Will Reichard
doNotChase.lead: The weekly kicker comparison, and this is the one where the honest answer is uncomfortable: two free agents outrank your kicker and you still should not move.

case.label: The board
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 rankings: Cam Little K3, Tyler Loop K4, Will Reichard K5, Chase McLaughlin K6, Tyler Bass K8, Jason Myers K9, Eddy Pineiro K12, Chris Boswell K17. Reichard and McLaughlin are both free agents here, so the upgrade would cost no priority — only a roster move.

case.label: The part that stings
case.body: Cam Little is K3, four spots above the kicker you replaced him with, and he is on waivers clearing at 01:00 tonight. Re-claiming him would spend season-long waiver priority on a kicker, which STRATEGY section 6 rules out in every branch. The drop on 18 September cost you the best kicker on the board and there is no cheap way back.

case.label: Why hold anyway
case.body: This seat changed hands at 07:06 on 18 September, which is inside the seven-day churn window. Rotating a kicker seat through a third occupant in four days to chase four ranking places is the exact pattern STRATEGY section 3 was written to stop, and the expected gain is well under a point.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers finishing outside the top twenty in Week 2 while Reichard or McLaughlin finish top five. The seat reopens on 22 September when the churn window expires, and the answer then is whoever tops that week's board as a free agent.

doNotChase.sources: Pro Football Network · ESPN league activity log · STRATEGY.md sections 3 and 6

doNotChase.name: Rams D/ST
doNotChase.lead: The weekly defence comparison. The highest-owned free agent in the league is a defence, and it is still not an upgrade.

case.label: The board
case.body: Yahoo's Week 2 tiers put Baltimore and the Rams in the same Tier 2, alongside New England, Pittsburgh and Jacksonville. Tier 1 is Philadelphia, San Francisco, Seattle and Tampa Bay, none of which are available here. The Chargers and Packers are Tier 3; Cleveland, Chicago and Detroit are Tier 5, 'avoid'.

case.label: Why Baltimore holds
case.body: They host New Orleans, who start Tyler Shough. Moving from a Tier 2 defence in a good matchup to another Tier 2 defence is a lateral move that costs a roster spot and gains nothing measurable.

case.label: The priority note that ends it
case.body: The Rams are a free agent, so this would not cost priority. It would still cost the seat, and the standing thesis is explicit: never spend waiver priority on a defence in this league regardless of what any board says.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Baltimore finishing outside the top twelve defensive scores in Week 2. The seat then reopens and the Rams are first on the list, because they are the only Tier 2 defence free here with a Monday night game you can see coming.

doNotChase.sources: Yahoo Sports Week 2 D/ST tiers · ESPN

doNotChase.name: Zach Charbonnet
doNotChase.lead: Your own player from 36 hours ago, back on the wire and clearing at 01:00 tonight. Familiarity is not a signal.

case.label: The status
case.body: He left this roster at 16:29 on 18 September and entered the wire on WAIVERS, clearing 07:00Z on 20 September. He is listed OUT with a week-2 projection of 0.0, and the league file's own known limitation is that projections are not zeroed reliably — here they are, which agrees with the designation.

case.label: Why claiming is strictly dominated
case.body: If nobody claims him he becomes a free agent at 01:00 and costs nothing at all. If Seattle publish a dated return he can be re-added then for nothing. Every branch where you want him is a branch where waiting is cheaper, and a claim would spend season-long priority on a player who is ruled out this week.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Seattle publishing a return date and activating him. At that point he is a free agent and the only question is the seat, which is the same question every other name on this page runs into.

cannotSee.label: This file is 48 minutes old, which is outside the freshness window
cannotSee.body: The IPADE publisher stamped 21:37 UTC against Chem's 21:52. The runbook's threshold is about 30 minutes, so this brief is built on data that may already be stale — in particular any waiver or roster move made in this league in the last three quarters of an hour is invisible to it. Nothing here is wrong because of it, but Rico Dowdle's status is the one thing I would re-check in the app before 01:00.

cannotSee.label: Whether Rico Dowdle gets claimed before you at 01:00 tonight
cannotSee.body: ESPN only ever returns your own pending claims. Team 13 sit at priority 2 with only McCaffrey, Corum and Rachaad White at running back and are the obvious claimant; Furia Regia at priority 1 just dropped him, so they are not. That is a read on their rosters rather than information. The recommendation is not to claim, so this matters less than it would otherwise — but it is why the free-agent branch may never open.

cannotSee.label: Whether a failed waiver claim costs priority here
cannotSee.body: I believe an unsuccessful claim leaves priority intact in ESPN, which would make a losing Dowdle bid free. I could not verify that against this league's settings, for a fifth run running, and the Dowdle row above is written as though a claim costs priority whether or not it lands. If that belief is right, the case for bidding is stronger than this brief makes it — and that is a gap in my information, not a hedge.

cannotSee.label: ESPN has a wrong injury designation on a rival's roster and it is not the only one
cannotSee.body: Josh Jacobs sits on two rosters in your two leagues carried as DAY_TO_DAY at 0.0. He has been on the Commissioner's Exempt List since 31 August and is not day-to-day in any sense. The league file's own known limitation is that projections are not zeroed reliably for unavailable players; this is the mirror of it, a designation that is stale rather than a projection that is stale. It is why MarShawn Lloyd's detail line is written from reporting rather than from the file.

cannotSee.label: One tile is dashed, and two more are graded on weaker evidence than they look
cannotSee.body: MarShawn Lloyd is dashed: nobody has published a Jets-against-backs number two games in. Two others are graded but thinly — Saquon Barkley rests on a Week 1 Titans rushing line because the film piece I found is blocked to automated readers, and Jason Myers rests on a kicker ranking rather than any Seattle or Arizona scoring-environment reporting, which I have now failed to retrieve on five consecutive runs. That last one is a standing gap in this brief, not a one-off.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are frozen, which undercuts the trade arithmetic
cannotSee.body: The Lamar deal has returned the identical +40.6 for Team 13 since 17 September, days apart, and tonight's Chem pair search returned the same zero as the 17 September one. That is what a preseason artifact looks like. The +3.4 weekly gain on the trade is real; treat the +11.6 season figure as August's opinion.

cannotSee.label: The two leagues do not score the same thing
cannotSee.body: Both are full PPR, but IPADE scores sacks at 4 to Chem's 3, uses defensive points-allowed tiers of 5/4/3/2 against Chem's 10/7/4/1, and scores six categories Chem does not. Quarterback and defence numbers diverge by five to six per cent between the files. Nothing on this page was computed from the Chem snapshot.
